simple.meaning: שְׁחִין (shᵉchîyn) is a Hebrew animal word meaning “inflammation , i.e. an ulcer.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Exodus 9:9. The surrounding context includes kingship, priesthood, land, Egypt.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to שְׁחִין (H7822) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: שְׁחִין (shᵉchîyn) / H7822 is traced through Exodus 9:9, Exodus 9:10, Exodus 9:11, Leviticus 13:18 with generated occurrence evidence.

timeline.evidenceText: It shall become small dust over all the land of Egypt, and shall be a boils and blisters breaking out on man and on animal, throughout all the land of Egypt.”
They took ashes of the furnace, and stood before Pharaoh; and Moses sprinkled it up toward the sky; and it became boils and blisters breaking on man and on animal.
The magicians couldn’t stand before Moses because of the boils; for the boils were on the magicians and on all the Egyptians.
The magicians couldn’t stand before Moses because of the boils; for the boils were on the magicians and on all the Egyptians.
“When the body has a boil on its skin, and it has healed,
and in the place of the boil there is a white swelling, or a bright spot, reddish-white, then it shall be shown to the priest.

The priest shall examine it. Behold, if its appearance is deeper than the skin, and its hair has turned white, then the priest shall pronounce him unclean. It is the plague of leprosy. It has broken out in the boil.
But if the bright spot stays in its place, and hasn’t spread, it is the scar from the boil; and the priest shall pronounce him clean.
Yahweh will strike you with the boils of Egypt, with the tumors, with the scurvy, and with the itch, of which you can not be healed.
Yahweh will strike you in the knees and in the legs with a sore boil, of which you cannot be healed, from the sole of your foot to the crown of your head.
Isaiah said, “Take a cake of figs.”
So Satan went out from the presence of Yahweh, and struck Job with painful sores from the sole of his foot to his head.
Now Isaiah had said, “Let them take a cake of figs, and lay it for a poultice on the boil, and he shall recover.”

definitions.full: H7822. shechin שְׁחִין noun masculine boil , collective eruption ; — on man 2Kin 20:7 = Isa 38:21 , ׳שׁ רָ֑ע Deut 28:35 ; Job 2:7 ; possibly leprous Lev 13:18-19 , 20 , הַשּׁ ׳צָרֶ֫בֶת 13:23 (see ׳צ ; all P), in Egypt, on man and beast Exod 9:9-10 , 11 (twice in verse) (all P), construct מִצְרַיִם שְׁחִין Deut 28:27 . שׁחף (√ of שַׁחֶפֶת and possibly of שַׁחַף ; Arabic is pare, peel off ; also affect with consumption of lungs; consumption , so Jewish-Aramaic שַׁחַפְתָּא [for שַׁחֶפֶת ]).
definitions.rootNote: from an unused root probably meaning to burn;
